GER 1105.title: Elementary German
GER 1105.description: Fundamentals of the German language with emphasis on grammar, reading, composition, and conversation. 1105: for students with no prior knowledge of the language; 1106: for students who have completed 1105 or less than three years in high school.

GER 1106.title: Elementary German
GER 1106.description: Fundamentals of the German language with emphasis on grammar, reading, composition, and conversation. 1105: for students with no prior knowledge of the language; 1106: for students who have completed 1105 or less than three years in high school.

GER 1114.title: Accelerated Elementary German
GER 1114.description: Proficiency-oriented approach to elementary German, designed for learners who wish to progress rapidly through the beginning stages of language learning. It develops the four language skills (speaking, listening, reading, writing) in a cultural context. Partially duplicates GER 1105 and 1106.

GER 2105.title: Intermediate German
GER 2105.description: Review of grammar with increasing emphasis on reading, writing, and oral communication.

GER 2106.title: Intermediate German
GER 2106.description: Review of grammar with increasing emphasis on reading, writing, and oral communication. I,II

GER 2114.title: Accelerated Intermediate German
GER 2114.description: Proficiency-oriented approach to intermediate German, designed for learners who wish to progress rapidly through the intermediate stages of language learning. The course strengthens the four language skills (speaking, listening, reading and writing) in a cultural context. Accelerated version of GER 2105-2106.

GER 2724.title: German Culture under Fascism and Its Legacy
GER 2724.description: Introduction to German Culture under Fascism and Its Legacy from 1933 to 1945 and its effects until today. Introduction to key individuals, groups, and institutions that shaped cultural production during the Third Reich. Analysis of the propagandistic dimension of major musical, cinematic, literary, theatrical, artistic, and architectural works. Interpretation of political and social contexts, including fascism, nationalism, antisemitism, and authoritarianism. Tracing of fascist and antisemitic ideology in contemporary German culture. Intercultural comparison of German and U.S. cultures of memory as they pertain to World War II and the Holocaust in order to sensitize students to the historical and cultural contexts of memory and remembrance. Taught in English.

GER 3105.title: Grammar, Composition and Conversation
GER 3105.description: Progressive and comprehensive review of German syntax and morphology. Development of written and oral expression. Development of reading and listening skills and introduction to contemporary public debates through the study of original German materials. Understanding of the role of social, historical, political, and cultural contexts and of fact- based reasoning in communication. Introduction to cultural research in German. Taught in German. GER 3105: review of basic and complex grammatical structures; GER 3106: review of advanced grammatical structures, writing intensive.

GER 3106.title: Grammar, Composition and Conversation
GER 3106.description: Progressive and comprehensive review of German syntax and morphology. Development of written and oral expression. Development of reading and listening skills and introduction to contemporary public debates through the study of original German materials. Understanding of the role of social, historical, political, and cultural contexts and of fact- based reasoning in communication. Introduction to cultural research in German. Taught in German. GER 3105: review of basic and complex grammatical structures; GER 3106: review of advanced grammatical structures, writing intensive.

GER 3204.title: Culture of the German-Speaking Countries
GER 3204.description: Study of German, Austrian, and Swiss culture and civilization from the Middle Ages to the present, including literature, art, architecture, film, and music.

GER 3214.title: German in a Globalized World
GER 3214.description: Overview of globalization and its impact on society, culture, politics, economy, and environment in the context of German-speaking countries, with a focus on Germany. Examination of the function and circulation of German within the European Union and in global contexts. Analysis of German-language texts, films, and cultural artifacts. Enhancement of German proficiency, intercultural competencies, and research skills. Taught in German.

GER 3305.title: Topics in German Culture and Literature
GER 3305.description: Introduces students to critical issues in German culture and literature. Familiarizes students with artistic, cultural, and socio-historical contexts necessary to analyze artifacts (canonical and non-canonical literature, film, art, architecture, and music). Develops critical reading, writing, speaking, and listening skills in German regarding complex texts, contexts, and concepts. Fosters cross-cultural awareness and intercultural sensitivity. 3305: examines pre-20th-century German cultural and literary developments; 3306: examines cultural and literary developments in the 20th and 21st centuries. Taught in German. Variable content. May be repeated once for credit with different content for a maximum of 6 credits.
GER 3305.prereq: (GER 3105 and GER 3106) or (GER 3105 and GER 3204) or (GER 3105 and GER 3306) or (GER 3106 and GER 3204) or (GER 3106 and GER 3306)

GER 3306.title: Topics in German Culture and Literature
GER 3306.description: Introduces students to critical issues in German culture and literature. Familiarizes students with artistic, cultural, and socio-historical contexts necessary to analyze artifacts (canonical and non-canonical literature, film, art, architecture, and music). Develops critical reading, writing, speaking, and listening skills in German regarding complex texts, contexts, and concepts. Fosters cross-cultural awareness and intercultural sensitivity. 3305: examines pre-20th-century German cultural and literary developments; 3306: examines cultural and literary developments in the 20th and 21st centuries. Taught in German. Variable content. May be repeated once for credit with different content for a maximum of 6 credits.

GER 3474.title: Topics in German Cinema
GER 3474.description: Critical issues in the history of German Cinema. Aesthetic characteristics of major periods, with an emphasis on cinematic trends and ways in which films reflect cultural developments in German-speaking countries. Taught in English. Variable content. May be taken twice for credit with different content.

GER 4154.title: Topics in German for Professional and Personal Communication
GER 4154.description: Professional and personal communication to acquire advanced linguistic and cultural proﬁciency in German. Analysis and writing of informal and formal texts, including job applications, workplace documents, and creative expressions of personal relevance. Composition and oral presentation on career related topics and intercultural discourses. Application of professional vocabulary as well as cultural idioms and conventions. Variable topics such as “German for Global Careers” or “German for International Affairs, Diplomacy, and Tourism”. Taught in German. May be repeated 1 time with different content for a maximum of 6 credits.

GER 4324.title: Studies in 20th-Century Literature
GER 4324.description: A variable content course devoted to the study of major literary works of the 20th century. May be repeated for credit with different content.

GER 4334.title: Special Topics in German Life, Literature, and Language
GER 4334.description: Variable content course devoted to the study of various aspects of German culture, literature, and language. May be repeated for credit with different content.
GER 4334.prereq: (GER 3105 and GER 3106) and (GER 3204 or GER 3305 or GER 3306)

GER 4794.title: Senior Tutorial in German Studies
GER 4794.description: Individual or small group sessions which give the student the opportunity to hone special language skills, with a focus on post-graduation application of these skills. May concentrate on areas such as technical or business language, linguistics, translation, interpreting, creative writing, specialized literary, or cultural studies. Must be pre-arranged three weeks before end of previous semester. May be taken twice for credit with different content. PRE: one 4000-level German course, major with senior standing, and consent required.

GER 5334G.title: Advanced Special Topics in German Life, Literature, and Language
GER 5334G.description: Variable content course devoted to the study of various aspects of German culture, literature, and language, such as the history of the German language, aesthetic movements, philosophical trends, or the staging of dramatic works in German. Includes related cultural theory and criticism. May be taken twice for credit with different content. Graduate Standing required
